newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sands, IPC hit gas at Malaysian block.
newsitem.headline: Sands, IPC hit gas at Malaysian block.

text.p: Sweden's Sands Petroleum and International Petroleum Company (IPC) said on Tuesday their first production test at an offshore Malaysian block found gas and condensate.
Bunga Seroja-1 in block PM-3 offshore Malaysia flowed at 50 million cubic feet of gas a day and 1,200 barrels condensate, Sands said in a statement.
"The test results to date indicate that the quantities of gas reserves in block PM-3 will increase substantially," Sands said.
Drilling has reached a depth of 6,988 feet.
Carbon dioxide in the gas was less than one percent which means the gas is very good quality, Sands said.
Bunga Seroja-1 is the first prospect drilling carried out to test the 'channel-sands' in block PM-3 and more product tests will be carried out in the near future.
The company said other similar 'channel-sands' have been identified in the block and following the good results from Bunga Seroja-1 more exploration and valuation drillings are planned.
"We have about five or six different drilling targets of a similar nature to Bunga Seroja," Sands' managing director Magnus Nordin told Reuters.
He said more drilling would go ahead between August and October this year.
Sands was expecting to release a full valuation of the reserves with the company's annual results next year.
Sands owns 15 percent of block PM-3 while IPC has 26.44 percent and is the operator.
Other partners are Malaysia's state owned Petronas Carigali Sdn Bhd with 46.06 percent and Vietnam's state-owned Petrovietnam Exploration and Production with 12.5 percent.
